title: Claim
description: One assertion, from one Document, about one thing, at one time (WO-047 / Issue #89, design in Issue #88 comment 2 Section 6). A Claim always names the Document it came from -- the traceability guarantee -- and may be attached to zero, one or (after a split) more than one logistics_event via event_ids. See docs/situation_intelligence_architecture.md.

source_id.description: Denormalised from the Document, for query and rights checks without a join. Must agree with document_id's own source_id -- enforced in scripts/validate.py, not the schema, matching the house pattern for cross-record checks.

document_id.description: Required. A claim with no document cannot exist -- this is the traceability guarantee.

event_ids.description: 0..n. A claim may be unattached (freshly extracted), attached to one Development, or -- deliberately -- attached to two after a split.

claim_text.description: A factual paraphrase authored by the platform, not an extract. Bounded to the same 600-character cap already enforced on event_evidence.claim, so the Claim x Document -> event_evidence adapter is lossless.

assertion.description: Structured triple where extractable; the prose fallback in claim_text is always retained regardless. Every part nullable.

measurement.description: Nullable-by-default: value is non-null iff value_status is 'available'. This is how a numeric claim in prose can later join the structured-evidence model.

corroboration_status.description: Default 'not_assessed', which is never treated as corroborated.

contradiction_status.description: Default 'none'. Mirrors logistics_event.conflicting_evidence[].resolution_status with an added 'none' state for a claim that is not part of any contradiction.

confidence.description: Reuses the impact_assessment.confidence vocabulary deliberately, so the platform has one confidence scale.

evidence_layer.description: Copied from the Document and frozen on the claim, so a later registry reclassification cannot retroactively promote a published L3 claim to L1. The L3 firewall's enforcement point.

primary_for_this_claim.description: Per-assertion primary/secondary. A carrier is primary about its own omission and secondary about the canal it transits.

independence_group.description: Copied from the Document, frozen. Corroboration counts distinct values here.

attributed_to.description: Present when the document attributes the assertion to someone else. is_named: false means the claim can never exceed REPORTED.

thailand_relevance_asserted.description: Prevents a regional claim silently becoming Thailand evidence.

claim_scope.description: Reuses event_evidence.scope_supported's vocabulary. A region-scope claim can never alone support a Thailand-scope conclusion.

permitted_by.description: Reference to the Document's rights.quotation_allowed basis when used is true. Cross-record agreement with the Document is checked in scripts/validate.py, not this schema, since a Claim does not embed its Document.

known_limitations.description: Mandatory; an empty array is a legal but reviewable value.

allOf.description: Reproducibility of an AI extraction (Issue #88 comment 2 Section 6.2): both fields required and non-null when extraction_method is one of the two ai_ values.
